subsystems.name: Front end
subsystems.role: fetches and decodes instructions so the rest of the core knows what to do.

subsystems.name: Execution core
subsystems.role: performs the actual arithmetic, logic and data movement.

subsystems.name: Cache hierarchy
subsystems.role: keeps frequently used data close to the core so it does not wait on main memory.

subsystems.name: Memory and I/O interfaces
subsystems.role: connects the CPU to RAM and to devices such as SSDs and graphics cards.

subsystems.name: Clock and power management
subsystems.role: sets the operating frequency and voltage, and throttles to stay within thermal limits.

subsystems.name: Package
subsystems.role: protects the silicon and connects it to the motherboard.

buildSteps.title: Design the architecture
buildSteps.detail: Define the instruction set, number of cores and cache sizes, then write the logic in a hardware description language.

buildSteps.title: Verify and synthesise
buildSteps.detail: Simulate billions of test cases to catch bugs, then convert the design into a gate-level netlist and place-and-route the transistors.

buildSteps.title: Make photomasks
buildSteps.detail: Every layer of the chip needs a master pattern. The smallest layers are written with extreme-ultraviolet lithography using 13.5 nm light.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate wafers
buildSteps.detail: Grow a silicon crystal, slice it into 300 mm wafers, then repeat lithography, etching, deposition and doping hundreds of times to build up transistors and wiring.

buildSteps.title: Test and dice
buildSteps.detail: Probe each die on the wafer to mark working ones, then cut the wafer into individual dies.

buildSteps.title: Package
buildSteps.detail: Attach good dies to a substrate, add a heat spreader and form the socket interface.

buildSteps.title: Bin and final test
buildSteps.detail: Test each finished CPU at different speeds and voltages, label it accordingly and ship it.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into a system
buildSteps.detail: Mount it in a motherboard socket, add cooling, and load firmware and an operating system.

pathway.milestone: multi-core processors at 3–5 nm nodes, often built as chiplets
pathway.unlocks: high performance per watt for laptops, servers and phones.

pathway.milestone: gate-all-around transistors and backside power delivery
pathway.unlocks: better control of current and lower voltage loss at smaller sizes.

pathway.milestone: 3D stacking of logic and cache, plus more on-die accelerators
pathway.unlocks: more memory bandwidth and faster special-purpose tasks without raising clock speed.

pathway.milestone: optical interconnects and new channel materials
pathway.unlocks: continued scaling if silicon transistors reach their physical limits.
